title: Convolutional Learnable-Group Weightless Neural Network
claim: Inputs are encoded into bits, passed through layers of interconnected lookup tables, and aggregated by group sums into class outputs.
layout: Single panel, left-to-right, dashed module boxes, LUT truth-table zoom inset
description: A single left-to-right architecture diagram. On the left is a photo of a pink cosmos flower. Arrows fan out from it to a dashed box labeled Binary Encoding, which holds eight rounded threshold nodes (>5.6, >4.3, >3.5, >2.1, >3.9, >1.2, >1.1, >0.6). The nodes are colored in pairs: yellow, teal, pink and blue. Thin black wires cross irregularly from these nodes into a dashed WNN box. The WNN box has two columns of four square LUT blocks, joined by dense criss-crossing connections. The outputs of the second column feed two circled plus nodes inside a dashed GroupSum box. Each plus node has an output arrow on the right. At the lower right, a dashed zoom-in leads from one LUT to an inset truth table of eight 0/1 cells, with input arrows on the left and an output arrow on the right. The eye goes first to the colorful encoding nodes and the tangle of wires.
caption: Architecture of WNN.
abstract: Weightless Neural Networks (WNNs) based on interconnected Lookup Tables (LUTs) have attracted attention for inference in extremely compact models, but achieving competitive accuracy under such tight resource budgets remains challenging. To address these issues, we introduce the Convolutional Learnable-Group Weightless Neural Network (CLGN). CLGN constructs convolutional layers using LUTs and incorporates a learnable GroupSum connection, thereby enhancing the accuracy of WNNs while maintaining low implementation resource consumption. Moreover, we propose a hierarchical training strategy to improve the training efficiency. We evaluate CLGN in two edge computing scenarios: (1) FPGA, where we evaluate accuracy, latency, throughput, power consumption, LUTs usage, and parameter size; and (2) Microprocessor, where we evaluate latency and memory usage. Compared with the state-of-the-art solutions, the proposed CLGN achieves superior accuracy while maintaining lower implementation resource consumption.
